about: Fixtures for the format adapters (F-items). The mapping spec:
https://github.com/o3co/xx.hocon/blob/main/docs/format-ingestion-mapping.md
Unlike expected/hocon/, these expectations are NOT generated from Lightbend.
Lightbend has no equivalent of these adapters, so there is no oracle: the
expectations encode the project's own F-item decisions, and the differential
value is that the four implementations agree with them and with each other.
They live under testdata/ rather than expected/ for that reason, and because
`make clean` deletes generated JSON.
YAML fixtures deliberately quote any scalar whose resolution differs between
YAML 1.1 and 1.2 (010, no, 1:30 and friends). Scalar resolution belongs to
the YAML library in use, not to this spec, so asserting on those forms would
test the library rather than the adapter. See F5 'Scope'.
The `properties` format was added after the first four, so a runner that
predates it hits its unknown-format branch (a panic or throw in all four).
A new format value is not a xx.hocon-only change: each runner needs a
dispatch arm for it.
Two reading rules the runner must honour, because two cases are silently
vacuous otherwise: read the input verbatim (fi24 turns on a lone CR, which
universal-newline text reads rewrite), and do not decode the BOM away
(fi17 and fi51 need the U+FEFF to reach the adapter, so no utf-8-sig).
Schema, runner contract and the F-items that deliberately have no fixture
(F1.9, F5.1, F5.3 on the parse path): docs/fixture-conventions.md,
'Format-ingestion fixtures'.

cases.note: F1.1/F1.2/F1.3 prefix filter, __ separator, lowercased segments
F1.6 two names reach one path and the environment has no order to break the tie
F1.7 the small dialect; ${x} inside single quotes stays literal (F0.2)
F1.7 a trailing # is refused rather than guessed at

F1.2 only __ creates hierarchy: a literal . in a variable name is key text, so APP_FOO.BAR is the single top-level key "foo.bar" and coexists with APP_FOO__BAR (two segments) instead of colliding with it under F1.6. Requires the mapped path to be carried as a segment list end-to-end — joining on . and re-splitting manufactures a boundary the environment never had.

F1.3 case folding is ASCII-only: A-Z lowercase, every other codepoint is left alone. APP_İ (U+0130) must not collide with APP_I under F1.6, and APP_K (U+212A KELVIN SIGN) must not collide with APP_K — full Unicode lowercasing folds both away, and it folds them differently per language (Go's simple mapping turns U+0130 into i, everyone else's full mapping into i + U+0307), so the mapping is pinned rather than inherited from each stdlib.

F2.9 no key denylist on the shared key-nesting path: constructor and prototype are ordinary keys, at the root and nested. __proto__ cannot be reached through env at all — it begins and ends with the __ separator, so it would map to empty segments — which is why fi50 pins it through properties.

F0.9 a leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped rather than glued to the first key. Left in place it yields the key "\ufefffoo", so a lookup of foo misses and the value is silently unreachable — the plausible-but-wrong output F0.9 exists to prevent.

F1.7 the prefix filter runs before validation, and export may be followed by a run of spaces and/or tabs. The OTHER= line carries a trailing comment this dialect refuses, and must never be inspected because it sits outside the mount — a .env shared with tools that do support trailing comments has to stay loadable for the slice the caller actually asked for. The two export lines use a tab and three spaces respectively: matching "export " alone turned the tab-separated line into the key "export<TAB>app_foo", silently.

F1.7 whitespace in a name means the Unicode White_Space property, pinned rather than inherited from each stdlib. U+0085 (NEL) is the codepoint that separates the four convenience predicates: Go unicode.IsSpace, Rust char::is_whitespace and Python str.isspace all have it, JavaScript regex \s does not — so this line errored in three implementations and produced the key foo<NEL>bar in ts.hocon. The mirror difference is Python-only: str.isspace reports U+001C-U+001F as space where White_Space does not, so those stay ordinary name characters. A plain space in a name is the uncontroversial core of the same rule and is covered by per-impl tests rather than a second fixture.
F3.2 line and block comments, trailing commas
comment markers inside string literals are data; F0.2 ${...} stays literal
F0.3 a config root must be an object

F3.2 comment stripping is token-separating: a comment is replaced by whitespace, never the empty string, so 1/*x*/2 stays two tokens and fails the JSON decode instead of silently reading as 12. No cites — the message is the underlying JSON decoder's and differs per implementation.

F3.2 a // comment ends at LF *or* CR. The input separates the comment from "b" with a lone CR (0x0D). Scanning only for \n makes the comment swallow that line, and because the trailing-comma pass then tidies the dangling comma the document still parses — losing the key "b" with no error at all. CAVEAT: a harness that reads the input in text mode with universal-newline translation (Python's Path.read_text default) turns the CR into an LF before the adapter sees it and the case passes vacuously; read the fixture as bytes, or with newline="", to keep it load-bearing.

F3.2 the mirror image of fi24: U+2028 deliberately does NOT terminate a // comment. node-jsonc-parser, which defines this dialect, treats only LF and CR as line breaks, so the comment runs through the U+2028 and "b" is commented out — the document is {"a":1,"c":3}. Ending the comment early would make the file mean one thing in the editor that owns the format and another here.
F4.2 HOCON has no datetime, so all four TOML date-time types are strings
F4.4 arrays of tables become arrays of objects; F0.2 ${...} stays literal
F0.6 infinity is not representable in HOCON
F5.2 aliases and merge keys resolve before mapping; an explicit key wins over a merged one, and no << may survive

F5.3 non-string scalar keys stringify. The integer and boolean keys sit in separate mappings on purpose: Python's bool subclasses int, so 1 and true collide as dict keys and a document with both as siblings is not representable there — a language-natural divergence, like S1.2.6. The quoted 010 and no are deliberate; see 'about'.
F5.7 decoding the first document and dropping the rest would be silent data loss
F5.9 an empty document is the empty object, as an empty HOCON document is (S3.1)
F5.5 HOCON has no binary type, so !!binary keeps its base64 text
F0.6 NaN is not representable in HOCON

F2.9 no key denylist: __proto__, constructor and prototype survive as ordinary keys, at the root and under a dotted parent. Dropping them would be data loss; JS implementations get prototype-pollution safety by construction (null-prototype carriers, own-property definition), never by dropping keys.

F0.9 a leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped rather than glued to the first key. This is the flat-format shape of the failure: left in place the key is "\ufeffa", so a lookup of a misses and the value is silently unreachable.
F2.1/F2.2/F2.4 baseline for the format: dotted keys nest, all values are strings, = / : / whitespace all separate, # and ! comment, \: is an escaped key character. F0.2 ${a.b} stays literal.
